title: 12 Best Tsukemen (Dipping Ramen) in Tokyo
description: The best tsukemen spots in Tokyo, curated from Reddit and food blogs. From legendary Fuunji to the birthplace of tsukemen at Taishoken — thick broths, chewy noodles, and honest reviews.

venues.name: Fuunji (風雲児)
venues.verdict: The single most recommended tsukemen in Tokyo across all of Reddit. Rich gyokai (fish) + pork broth that defines the modern tsukemen standard.
venues.whatToOrder: Tsukemen with the large noodle size (same price). Add ajitama. Ask for soup-wari to finish the broth as a drink.
venues.insiderTip: The line looks intimidating but moves fast — usually 15-20 minutes. Go right at open (11 AM) for shortest wait.

venues.name: Menya Itto (麺屋 一燈)
venues.verdict: Consistently ranked in Japan's top 3 tsukemen. The broth is extremely rich and concentrated — a pilgrimage-worthy bowl.
venues.whatToOrder: Tokuseizenbu-nose tsukemen (special topping tsukemen). The chashu and ajitama are exceptional.
venues.insiderTip: Worth the trek to Shin-Koiwa. Arrive before opening — the queue is real but orderly.

venues.name: Rokurinsha (六厘舎)
venues.address: 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda, Tokyo 100-0005 (Tokyo Ramen Street B1F)
venues.verdict: The most famous tsukemen in Tokyo — the shop that brought tsukemen to the mainstream. Ultra-thick tonkotsu gyokai broth.
venues.whatToOrder: Classic tsukemen with large noodles. The morning set (before 10 AM) is a hidden deal.
venues.insiderTip: Located in Tokyo Ramen Street beneath Tokyo Station. Opens at 7:30 AM for a rare breakfast ramen experience.

venues.name: Taishoken (大勝軒)
venues.verdict: The birthplace of tsukemen. Founded by Kazuo Yamagishi in 1961, this is where it all started. A pilgrimage for noodle historians.
venues.whatToOrder: Morisoba (the original tsukemen). Portions are famously large — the regular is already generous.
venues.insiderTip: Closed Wednesdays. The Google rating is lower because it's old-school and not flashy — the experience is historical, not trendy.

venues.name: Menya Sugo (麺屋 すごう)
venues.verdict: The highest-rated tsukemen in this list. Rich, balanced broth with bright red egg yolk and perfectly chewy thick noodles.
venues.whatToOrder: Tsukemen with all toppings. Ask them to thin the soup for drinking after you finish — they give you a platter of sides to mix in.
venues.insiderTip: They offer parasols while you wait in line to block the sun. Arrive at opening for no wait, otherwise expect 30-40 minutes.

venues.name: Gonokami Seisakujo (五ノ神製作所)
venues.verdict: Famous for their ebi (shrimp) tsukemen — a unique twist on the classic. The broth is creamy and intensely shrimpy.
venues.whatToOrder: Ebi tsukemen (shrimp dipping noodles). The ebi flavor is deep and unlike anything else in Tokyo.
venues.insiderTip: Near Shinjuku Gyoen. Combine with a park visit. Open all day with no break — great for off-peak lunch at 2-3 PM.

venues.name: Tsukemen Enji (つけ麺 えん寺)
venues.verdict: A tsukemen specialist loved by locals in West Tokyo. Known for their vegetable-based "vegepotage" tsukemen — uniquely creamy and satisfying.
venues.whatToOrder: Vegepotage tsukemen — a thick, creamy vegetable-infused broth that's lighter but still deeply savory.
venues.insiderTip: Rarely a long queue compared to central Tokyo spots. Pair with a walk through Inokashira Park nearby.

venues.name: Mensho Tokyo (麺庄 東京)
venues.verdict: An innovative shop known for creative lamb-based tsukemen and seasonal specials. Not traditional, but boundary-pushing.
venues.whatToOrder: Lamb tsukemen — the signature. Rich, gamey broth that's polarizing but unforgettable for adventurous eaters.
venues.insiderTip: Near Tokyo Dome. Great pre-game or post-event stop. Open all day — no lunch/dinner break.

venues.name: Dogenzaka Mammoth (道玄坂マンモス)
venues.verdict: Shibuya's go-to for thick, noukou-style tsukemen. The massive portions and concentrated broth make it a favorite among locals.
venues.whatToOrder: Tokumori (extra large) tsukemen. The broth is extremely thick and coating — perfect for cold dipping.
venues.insiderTip: Open straight through with no break. A solid late-night option open until 10 PM in the heart of Shibuya.

venues.name: Ginza Kagari (銀座 篝)
venues.verdict: Famous for their tori-paitan (chicken white soup). Their tsukemen version is rich, creamy, and refined — Ginza-level quality.
venues.whatToOrder: Tori-paitan tsukemen. The chicken broth is silky and deeply savory. Also try their soba (ramen) if you have room.
venues.insiderTip: Ranked #3 on Tabelog for Tokyo tsukemen. Expect a queue but it moves steadily. The Ginza location is the honten (main shop).

venues.name: Chuka Soba Tomita (中華蕎麦 とみ田)
venues.verdict: Widely considered the #1 tsukemen in all of Japan. Technically in Matsudo (Chiba) but an easy 30-minute train ride. The GOAT.
venues.whatToOrder: Tokuseizenbu-nose tsukemen. Every single element is perfected — noodles, broth, chashu, egg.
venues.insiderTip: Queue online — you can place your name and they give you an exact return time, so you can explore Matsudo while waiting.

venues.name: Kinryu (金竜)
venues.verdict: A hidden gem near Akihabara known for their tantan (spicy sesame) tsukemen and kombusui (kombu water) style — different from the norm.
venues.whatToOrder: Tantan tsukemen for spice lovers. The kombusui tsukemen is also excellent — lighter and more nuanced.
venues.insiderTip: Closes early at 8:30 PM. A great pitstop if you're exploring Akihabara or the Kanda area.
